risk.rationale: The system ranks and filters job applications for recruiters and evaluates candidates by relevance score. This is an employment/recruitment use under Annex III point 4(a). Human review of every decision does not remove that classification. The system does not use any Art. 5 prohibited practice: it uses no emotion recognition, no biometric data, and no social scoring. The README also states a high-risk position. The documentation gaps (bias examination not performed, TBD sections) are compliance issues and do not change the tier.
triggers: Annex III 4(a): AI used to analyse and filter job applications and evaluate candidates

requirements.title: No prohibited AI practices
requirements.statement: The system does not implement any practice prohibited by Art. 5(1): subliminal or manipulative techniques, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, crime prediction based solely on profiling, untargeted scraping of facial images, emotion inference in the workplace or in education, or biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits.

checks.description: no emotion recognition / social scoring / face scraping code

requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code or documentation showing the system infers emotions (e.g. from video interviews or voice) of employees/candidates/students, scores people on social behaviour, scrapes facial images, or categorises people by biometrics into sensitive traits. A comment or doc stating that such a feature is NOT implemented is evidence of compliance, not a violation. Mark non_compliant only if a prohibited practice is actually implemented or planned for production.

requirements.title: Risk classification documented
requirements.statement: The provider documents the AI Act risk classification of the system with its rationale: the applicable Annex III area/point if high-risk, the Art. 6(3) assessment if an Annex III system is claimed not to be high-risk, or why the system is limited/minimal risk.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept a README section, ADR or compliance document that states the risk tier AND gives a reason (e.g. "Annex III point 4(a) recruitment", "chatbot, transparency obligations under Art. 50", "spam filtering, no Annex III use case"). A bare marketing claim ("fully compliant") is not a classification.

requirements.title: Risk management system documented
requirements.statement: A risk management process is documented for the high-risk system: known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights are identified and evaluated, and targeted mitigation measures with residual-risk acceptance are recorded and kept up to date.

checks.description: a risk assessment / risk register document exists

requirements.llm_guidance: Look for a risk register / risk assessment / model risk management document listing concrete risks (e.g. discrimination, automation bias, data drift), their likelihood/impact and mitigations. A single sentence like "risks are low" is not sufficient (partial at most).

requirements.title: Training data documented (datasheet)
requirements.statement: Training, validation and test data sets are documented: origin and collection process, original purpose for personal data, preparation steps (labelling, cleaning, enrichment), assumptions, and the availability/quantity/suitability of the data.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept a datasheet / data card / training-data document. Code that loads a CSV is not documentation. Partial if only some of origin, preparation and splits are described.

requirements.title: Bias examination and mitigation of data sets
requirements.statement: The data sets have been examined for possible biases likely to lead to discrimination (including representativeness for the persons and setting the system is used on), and measures to detect, prevent and mitigate the identified biases are documented with results.
requirements.llm_guidance: Requires an actual bias/fairness analysis with results (metrics per group, findings, mitigations). A plan ("bias audit planned"), a TODO, or merely excluding protected attributes from the features does NOT satisfy this requirement on its own (proxies may remain). Judge from documents and evaluation code/reports.

requirements.title: Technical documentation (Annex IV)
requirements.statement: Technical documentation covering the Annex IV elements exists before deployment: general description and intended purpose, versions, how the system interacts with other software, development methods, design specifications and key design choices, system architecture, and validation/testing procedures.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant only if a document (or set of docs) covers most Annex IV(1)-(2) elements. An architecture overview plus a model card without development/validation information is partial.

requirements.title: Model card for the deployed model
requirements.statement: A model card documents the deployed model: intended use and out-of-scope uses, version, training data summary, evaluation results, capabilities and known limitations.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check that a model card exists and covers intended use, limitations and evaluation results.

requirements.title: Instructions for use for deployers
requirements.statement: Instructions for use are provided to deployers and contain at least: provider identity and contact, intended purpose, level of accuracy and its metrics, known limitations and foreseeable misuse risks, human oversight measures, and how to collect and interpret the logs.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant only if the instructions contain all the listed elements. If a guide exists but misses accuracy metrics, limitations or log interpretation, the status is partial. Sections marked TBD count as missing.

requirements.title: Interpretable outputs for deployers
requirements.statement: The system provides information that lets deployers interpret each output (e.g. main reasons, feature contributions, reason codes or confidence) rather than a bare score.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code that returns explanations/reason codes alongside the score and shows them to the human reviewer. A global feature-importance chart in a notebook alone is partial.

requirements.title: Disclosure of interaction with an AI system
requirements.statement: Natural persons interacting directly with the AI system (e.g. a chatbot) are informed, clearly and at the latest at the first interaction, that they are interacting with an AI system.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for user-facing UI strings (React/HTML templates, chat greeting) that tell users they talk to an AI, shown at the start of the conversation. A statement buried in terms of service is not sufficient.
evidence_queries: you are chatting with an AI

requirements.title: Marking of AI-generated content
requirements.statement: Synthetic text, image, audio or video generated by the system is marked as AI-generated in a machine-readable format (and labelled for the recipient where it is published or delivered).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code that adds an AI-generated flag/header/metadata or visible label to each generated message. A TODO or ticket reference to add labelling later means non_compliant. A disclosure that the user talks to an AI (Art. 50(1)) is a different obligation and does not mark the content.

requirements.title: Affected persons informed about high-risk AI use
requirements.statement: Natural persons subject to decisions made or assisted by the high-risk AI system (candidates, applicants, workers) are informed that such a system is used on them.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for a candidate/applicant notice, privacy notice or e-mail template that tells the person an AI system is used to assess them. Recruiter-facing UI text does not inform the candidate.

requirements.title: Automatic logging of AI decisions
requirements.statement: The system automatically records an event for each decision/output over its lifetime, with timestamp, input reference, output, model version and (where applicable) the human reviewer, enabling traceability and post-market monitoring.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for code that writes a structured record for every prediction (custom journal/audit classes count). Commented-out logging calls, TODOs or debug prints do not count. Logging only errors is not decision logging.

requirements.title: Logs retained for at least six months
requirements.statement: Automatically generated decision logs are retained for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and of at least six months (>= 180 days).
requirements.llm_guidance: Find the effective retention of the decision/audit logs (config, Terraform log group, lifecycle rules). Compliant only if >= 180 days. If logs exist but retention is shorter or unbounded deletion is configured, non_compliant. If no logs exist at all, non_compliant.

requirements.title: Human can override or disregard the AI output
requirements.statement: Natural persons overseeing the system can decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse an individual output of the system, and the override is recorded.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an implemented mechanism (API endpoint, UI action, workflow state) letting a human change the outcome. A flag set to False, a README promise without code, or an override limited to admins for model config does not count.

requirements.title: Stop / interrupt mechanism
requirements.statement: Operators can interrupt the system (a 'stop' button, kill switch or similar procedure) so that it halts in a safe state, e.g. automated processing is suspended and cases fall back to manual handling.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept any implemented switch (feature flag, admin endpoint, config) that stops automated decisions and routes work to humans. Infrastructure scaling to zero without a documented procedure is partial.

requirements.title: No adverse decision solely on the AI output
requirements.statement: Decisions adverse to natural persons (e.g. rejection, decline) are not taken automatically on the basis of the AI output alone; a competent human reviews and confirms them, mitigating automation bias.
requirements.llm_guidance: Trace the decision flow in code. If any adverse outcome is set without a human step (e.g. score below threshold -> rejected), it is non_compliant; if only a subset of cases gets human review (e.g. above an amount threshold), partial.

requirements.title: Accuracy levels and metrics declared
requirements.statement: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics (e.g. AUC, precision/recall, error rates) are declared in the documentation accompanying the system (instructions for use and/or model card).
requirements.llm_guidance: Metrics must be declared in documentation shipped with the system, with values. A training script that prints accuracy is not a declaration.

requirements.title: Resilience to errors (fallback / fail-safe)
requirements.statement: The system handles errors, faults and model unavailability safely (e.g. timeouts and exceptions lead to a fail-safe outcome such as routing to manual handling, never to an automatic adverse decision).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for explicit error handling around model inference with a safe fallback. Generic web framework error pages are not sufficient.

requirements.title: Input validation against malformed or adversarial inputs
requirements.statement: Inputs to the model are validated (schema, types, ranges, size limits, file types) before inference to resist malformed or adversarial inputs.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for schema validation (pydantic/zod/marshmallow), constraints and upload limits on the inference path. Reading raw request bodies directly into the model is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Protection of model endpoints against unauthorised use
requirements.statement: Inference and model-management endpoints are protected against unauthorised third parties (authentication and authorisation), so that the system's use, outputs or performance cannot be altered by exploiting vulnerabilities.
requirements.llm_guidance: Every inference and admin route must require authentication; admin/model routes need authorisation. Partial if some sensitive routes are unauthenticated.

requirements.title: Quality management and post-market monitoring procedures
requirements.statement: Documented procedures cover change management of the model/system, validation before release, post-market monitoring of performance in production (e.g. drift), and serious-incident reporting.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant if the repository documents change management, pre-release validation, production monitoring AND incident reporting; partial if only some are covered.

requirements.title: Testing against predefined metrics before release
requirements.statement: The system is tested before release against prior defined metrics and thresholds appropriate to its intended purpose (e.g. an automated quality gate failing the build below a minimum AUC).
requirements.llm_guidance: Smoke tests that only check an HTTP 200 are not model validation; require assertions against metric thresholds on held-out data.

requirements.title: Lawful basis documented for each processing purpose
requirements.statement: Each purpose for which personal data is processed has a documented lawful basis under Art. 6(1) (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task or legitimate interests), and consent is collected and recorded where it is the basis relied on.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for a privacy notice, record of processing or DPIA naming the lawful basis per purpose. A README claim "fully GDPR compliant" is not evidence of a lawful basis.

requirements.title: Privacy notice provided to data subjects
requirements.statement: Data subjects receive a privacy notice at collection stating the controller and contact details, purposes and lawful basis, recipients, retention period, and their rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection, complaint).
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant if a notice covering controller, purposes, legal basis, retention and rights exists and is shown/linked to data subjects. Partial if key items (e.g. retention or rights) are missing.
evidence_queries: how long we keep your data

requirements.title: Storage limitation enforced
requirements.statement: Personal data is kept no longer than necessary for its purpose: a retention period proportionate to the purpose is defined for each data category and enforced automatically (TTL, purge job, lifecycle rule).
requirements.llm_guidance: Check both that a retention period is defined AND enforced in code/IaC, and that it is proportionate (e.g. keeping raw support chats for years without justification is excessive; keeping data "forever" is non_compliant). Defined and enforced but disproportionate -> partial.

requirements.title: Right to erasure implemented
requirements.statement: A mechanism exists to erase a data subject's personal data on request without undue delay (endpoint, admin job or documented procedure covering all stores, including derived data).
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an implemented deletion path for a single data subject. Automatic expiry of all data after N days is not an on-request erasure mechanism (partial at most).

requirements.title: Safeguards for solely automated decisions
requirements.statement: Decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects are not based solely on automated processing, or, where an Art. 22(2) exception applies, the data subject can obtain human intervention, express their point of view and contest the decision.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant if no significant decision is fully automated, OR if automated decisions come with an implemented contest/appeal path leading to human review. Non_compliant if decisions are fully automated with no recourse.

requirements.title: Meaningful information about the logic involved
requirements.statement: Data subjects are informed of the existence of automated decision-making/profiling and receive meaningful information about the logic involved and its envisaged consequences.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for an applicant/candidate-facing explanation of the main factors used and the consequences. Internal model documentation does not inform data subjects.

requirements.title: Data minimisation and privacy by design
requirements.statement: Only personal data necessary for the purpose is collected and used (no unnecessary sensitive or protected attributes as model features), and privacy-by-design measures such as pseudonymisation or redaction are applied before processing or sharing with third parties.
requirements.llm_guidance: Inspect model features and data flows. Using gender/age/nationality as features, or sending raw personal data to a third-party LLM without redaction, is non_compliant. Look for explicit redaction/pseudonymisation code.

requirements.title: Encryption of personal data at rest and in transit
requirements.statement: Personal data is encrypted at rest (databases, object storage, volumes, backups) and in transit (TLS) as appropriate to the risk.
requirements.llm_guidance: Both at-rest and in-transit encryption must be evidenced for all stores holding personal data. Only one of the two -> partial. Self-signed dev certificates in docker-compose do not count for production.

requirements.title: Access control to personal data
requirements.statement: Access to personal data and to administrative functions is restricted to authenticated and authorised personnel (authentication, role-based authorisation, least privilege).
requirements.llm_guidance: Check that endpoints exposing personal data require authentication and that admin/export routes check roles. Unauthenticated upload/listing endpoints are non_compliant.

requirements.title: Record of processing activities
requirements.statement: A record of processing activities is maintained for the system listing purposes, categories of data subjects and personal data, recipients, transfers, retention limits and security measures.
requirements.llm_guidance: Accept a ROPA entry in the repo (markdown/yaml). A DPIA or privacy notice alone is not a ROPA but may be partial if it contains the Art. 30(1) items.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.statement: A DPIA has been carried out for the processing (systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing) and contains a description of the processing, necessity and proportionality assessment, risk assessment and mitigation measures.
requirements.llm_guidance: Compliant only if a DPIA document with the Art. 35(7) elements exists.

requirements.title: AI use disclosed in user interfaces
requirements.statement: Every interface where a person interacts with the AI system or sees an AI-produced score, ranking, classification or text visibly discloses AI involvement; decision-support UIs state that the output is an AI recommendation and who decides.
requirements.llm_guidance: Inspect UI components, e-mail templates and notification texts. Neutral names like "Smart Score" do not disclose AI involvement.

requirements.title: AI-generated content labelled
requirements.statement: AI-generated text/media delivered to customers carries a visible "AI-generated" label and, where feasible, a machine-readable marker.
requirements.llm_guidance: A banner saying the user chats with an AI is POL-1, not POL-2. Look for per-message labelling or metadata. TODO comments do not count.

requirements.title: Prediction logging with 180-day retention
requirements.statement: Every production prediction/response is logged with timestamp, correlation id, model version, input reference and output, in tamper-resistant storage retained for at least 180 days.
requirements.llm_guidance: Both parts are needed: structured per-prediction logging AND >= 180 days retention. Logging with shorter retention -> partial. No logging -> non_compliant.
evidence_queries: prediction log model version request id

requirements.title: Raw personal-data inputs deleted within 30 days
requirements.statement: Raw inputs containing personal data (documents, messages, transcripts, payloads) are automatically deleted or anonymised within 30 days, unless a documented legal retention obligation applies.
requirements.llm_guidance: Find the retention of each raw-input store. Any raw store kept > 30 days without a documented legal obligation is non_compliant; no automated deletion at all is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Encryption at rest and TLS in transit
requirements.statement: Storage of personal data, model artefacts and logs is encrypted at rest, and all service traffic uses TLS 1.2+.
requirements.llm_guidance: Both at rest and in transit must be shown; one of the two -> partial.

requirements.title: Access control on model endpoints
requirements.statement: Inference and model-management endpoints require authentication (or are declared public and rate-limited), and administrative endpoints enforce role-based authorisation.
requirements.llm_guidance: Enumerate routes. Any undeclared unauthenticated inference/upload route, or an admin route without a role check, is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Human approval of adverse decisions
requirements.statement: Adverse decisions about natural persons (rejection, decline, closure) are approved by a human reviewer who sees the AI output and reasons and can change the outcome, and the approval is logged.
requirements.llm_guidance: Trace adverse outcomes in code. Human approval for only part of the cases (e.g. above an amount threshold) is partial. Automatic rejection is non_compliant.

requirements.title: Model card for every deployed model
requirements.statement: Each deployed model (including third-party models) has a model card covering intended and out-of-scope use, version, training data summary, evaluation metrics, limitations and owner.
requirements.llm_guidance: Check presence and completeness of the model card(s) against the listed fields.

requirements.title: Rate limiting on AI endpoints
requirements.statement: AI endpoints reachable from untrusted networks enforce per-client rate limiting configured in code or configuration.
requirements.llm_guidance: Look for rate-limit middleware (express-rate-limit, slowapi), gateway throttling or ingress annotations. Public endpoints without it are non_compliant.

requirements.title: AI incident response procedure
requirements.statement: The repository contains an AI incident response procedure (detection, escalation, reporting) that requires reporting serious incidents to the AI Governance Board within 24 hours.
requirements.llm_guidance: A generic ops runbook without AI incidents or without the 24h governance reporting is partial.

requirements.title: Bias and fairness evaluation before release
requirements.statement: A documented bias and fairness evaluation (metrics and results per protected group, mitigations) exists for the released model and is referenced from the model card.
requirements.llm_guidance: Requires actual results. "Planned", TODOs or excluding protected features only is non_compliant.

verdicts.rationale: The system is a CV-ranking decision-support tool. The API docstring says emotion recognition and video or voice analysis are deliberately unsupported (Art. 5(1)(f)) and that only parsed CV text is used [E1]. The API input schema has only CV text fields (skills, experience, education, languages, summary) and no media inputs [E1][E7]. The model card lists use on video, audio or photos as out of scope [E5]. The datasheet shows photo, gender and nationality are removed from the training data [E8]. Nothing in the excerpts shows subliminal manipulation, vulnerability exploitation, social scoring, face scraping, crime prediction or biometric categorisation. Humans take every decision [E4][E2].
verdicts.remediation: Optional: add an explicit Art. 5 prohibited-practices screening section to docs/risk-assessment.md covering each of (a)-(h). Add a CI check that blocks emotion-recognition or face-scraping dependencies.

verdicts.rationale: docs/risk-assessment.md [E1] states the risk tier (high-risk) and gives the rationale: Annex III point 4(a), covering analysing and filtering job applications and evaluating candidates. It also addresses Art. 6(3) and explains that the derogation does not apply because the ranking materially influences decisions and the system profiles natural persons. The README [E2] repeats the classification and points to the rationale document. The technical documentation [E4] is consistent with it.
verdicts.remediation: No action needed for this requirement.

verdicts.rationale: E1 holds a dated risk register (reviewed 2026-06-20). It lists concrete risks to health, safety and fundamental rights: automation bias, drift, historical bias, parsing errors, unauthorised access and misuse. Each risk has likelihood, impact, targeted mitigation and residual level. The register is kept up to date (E1), and E5 describes post-market monitoring, drift alerts and quarterly reviews that feed it. Residual-risk acceptance is recorded: R-03 is explicitly marked "medium (not accepted yet)" while its fairness evaluation (HR-412) is pending (E1, E4, E6). The statement asks for recorded acceptance, and this honestly records a non-accepted risk, so the process is documented. The open R-03 is a substantive weakness, but it is not a missing element of the documented process.
gaps: R-03 (historical bias) residual risk is not yet accepted; the group fairness evaluation (HR-412) is pending
No explicit overall residual-risk acceptance sign-off visible
Reasonably foreseeable misuse is covered only for the promotion-decision case (R-06)
verdicts.remediation: Complete the group fairness evaluation (HR-412) before further release. Then update R-03 with the result and record a formal sign-off, with name and date, on each residual risk and on the overall residual risk in docs/risk-assessment.md. Add a review cadence and a link to post-market monitoring findings.

verdicts.rationale: DATASHEET.md [E1] documents the elements in the statement. It covers origin and collection (ACME ATS exports) and the original purpose for personal data (recruitment for the advertised role). It covers preparation (CV parsing, dedup, ESCO normalisation, label audit, field removal). It covers assumptions (shortlisting as a proxy for relevance). It covers availability, quantity and suitability (512k triples, 14 countries, under-representation in DE/AT). It also describes the train/validation/test splits. The missing bias examination falls under Art. 10(2)(f)/(g), which the statement does not ask for. [E2] and [E4] back up the documentation.
gaps: Bias examination not yet performed (HR-412). This is outside this requirement's statement but should be tracked separately.
verdicts.remediation: Complete the bias examination (HR-412) and add its results and mitigation measures to DATASHEET.md. Optionally, add a suitability assessment per split.

verdicts.rationale: No bias examination has been performed or documented with results. The datasheet says the bias examination is "not yet performed on this version" (ticket HR-412, planned Q4 2026) [E3]. The model card says the group-level fairness evaluation is not completed [E1]. The risk register lists R-03 as pending and not accepted [E2]. The only measure in place is removing protected fields [E2][E7][E4]. That does not satisfy the requirement, because proxies may remain. The datasheet notes some under-representation (DE/AT engineering) [E3], but there is no representativeness analysis or group metrics. The release gates cover only performance metrics [E8].
gaps: No bias/fairness analysis of the data sets has been performed (HR-412 pending)
No metrics per group (gender, age, origin) and no findings
No representativeness assessment against the persons and setting the system is used on
No proxy analysis after removing protected attributes
No documented detection, prevention or mitigation measures with results
No fairness gate in the release process
verdicts.remediation: Complete HR-412 before release. Run a group fairness analysis on the training and test data, and on the model outputs, with metrics per group (shortlist rate, selection-rate ratio, equal opportunity, NDCG by gender, age band, country and origin proxies). Check for proxy features, and assess representativeness by country, role family and language. Document findings and mitigations (reweighting, label audit, feature removal, thresholds) in DATASHEET.md, MODEL_CARD.md and a fairness report. Update risk R-03, and add a fairness check to the CI gate and release sign-off in docs/release-process.md. Add fairness monitoring to the weekly report.

verdicts.rationale: docs/technical-documentation.md (E1) is structured on Annex IV and covers the statement's elements. It gives the intended purpose, provider and version (2.4.1, with the previous version 2.3.0). It describes interaction with the ATS bridge and dashboard, software versions, deployment form, hardware and UI. It also covers development methods (LambdaRank, group CV), design choices and architecture. Validation and testing procedures are evidenced in docs/release-process.md (offline evaluation with CI gates, shadow deployment, go/no-go) and MODEL_CARD.md (evaluation metrics) (E8, E3). Data and design rationale are supported by DATASHEET.md (E4) and the risk assessment (E5). The excerpt of E1 is cut off, so any later sections are not visible, which is not treated as a gap. Open items such as the pending fairness evaluation and the TBD sections in the instructions for use (E6) concern other requirements or sub-elements beyond what the statement asks for.
gaps: Instructions for use sections on performance/limitations and logs are TBD (E6)
Fairness/bias evaluation not completed (E3, E4)
Technical documentation does not visibly cross-reference the validation procedure, which sits in docs/release-process.md
verdicts.remediation: Add a validation and testing section to docs/technical-documentation.md that links to docs/release-process.md and MODEL_CARD.md. Complete the TBD sections in docs/instructions-for-use.md. Finish the group fairness evaluation (HR-412) and document the results. Keep the document updated with each release.

verdicts.rationale: MODEL_CARD.md [E2] exists and documents the deployed model `ranker-2.4.1`. It covers intended use, out-of-scope uses, version, a training data summary (referencing DATASHEET.md [E5]), hold-out evaluation results (NDCG@10, AUC and others), and known limitations. The model version matches model.py [E9] and the technical documentation [E1]. The missing fairness evaluation is disclosed openly in the card and is not an element of this statement. The "TBD" sections in the instructions for use [E6] are a separate document.
verdicts.remediation: No change is needed for this requirement. Separately, complete the group fairness evaluation (HR-412) and update the model card's Fairness section. Fill in the TBD "Performance and limitations" section of docs/instructions-for-use.md.

verdicts.rationale: The instructions for use (E2) exist and cover provider identity and contact, intended purpose and human oversight (Move/override, suspension, training). Section 4 "Performance and limitations" is TBD, so accuracy metrics, known limitations and foreseeable misuse risks are missing. Section 5 "Logs" is also TBD, so there is nothing on how to collect or interpret logs. The journal is described only in the ADR (E9), which is not part of the deployer instructions. The misuse risk R-06 appears in the risk register (E5), but it is not in the instructions.
gaps: Accuracy level and metrics (section 4 is TBD)
Known limitations and foreseeable misuse risks (section 4 is TBD)
How to collect and interpret logs (section 5 is TBD)
verdicts.remediation: Fill in docs/instructions-for-use.md section 4 with the tested accuracy metrics (e.g. NDCG and recall@k, with datasets and conditions) and the known limitations. Include circumstances that reduce accuracy, such as unusual CV formats and parse failures. Add foreseeable misuse such as use for internal promotion decisions. Fill in section 5 with how to access the DecisionJournal, using the Athena view and the 400-day retention. Explain the event types (ranked, reviewer_decision, override, suspended, resumed) and the fields, and how to interpret them.

verdicts.rationale: The ranker computes per-candidate SHAP contributions and returns the top 5 reasons alongside the score (E1). The API records and returns these reasons (E6). The recruiter UI shows a "Main reasons" column with direction indicators next to each score (E2). The instructions for use tell recruiters how to read the reasons (E3), and the technical documentation describes per-candidate SHAP explanations (E4). This covers per-output interpretability for deployers, not just a bare score or a global chart.
gaps: UI shows only the direction of each reason, not the magnitude of its contribution (not required by the statement)
Performance and limitations section of the instructions for use is TBD (outside this requirement's core statement)
verdicts.remediation: Optionally show contribution magnitudes or confidence in the UI. Complete sections 4 and 5 of docs/instructions-for-use.md, including explanation limitations.

verdicts.rationale: Applies to limited risk systems; this system is classified as high.
Applies to limited risk systems; this system is classified as high.

The candidate privacy notice shown on the careers portal states "We use an AI system to rank applications by relevance to the job description" and that a recruiter takes all decisions (E3). This is candidate-facing and tells applicants that an AI system is used to assess them, which is what the statement requires. The README confirms candidates are informed through this notice (E2). The recruiter UI banner (E5) is not counted as evidence. The statement concerns candidates/applicants, and the evidence covers them.
gaps: No evidence of informing workers' representatives (Art. 26(7)), though the system is scope-limited to external applicants and the statement names candidates/applicants
Notice does not explicitly say it is a 'high-risk' AI system (not required by the statement)
verdicts.remediation: Optionally add an application-confirmation e-mail or portal checkbox repeating the AI-use notice, and document how worker representatives would be informed if the system's scope is extended to employees.

verdicts.rationale: The DecisionJournal writes a structured JSON entry per event to an object-locked S3 sink (E4, E8, E3). Each entry has an automatic UTC timestamp, a SHA-256 input digest as the input reference, the result (score and reasons), the model version, and the actor. The ranking endpoint records a "ranked" entry for each scoring call (E5). Recruiter decisions and overrides are also journaled with the reviewer's id (E5), which covers the human reviewer element. The ADR sets 400-day retention and supports traceability and post-market monitoring (E3).
verdicts.remediation: No action required. Optionally, add tests that assert a journal entry is written for every rank call, including the needs_manual_review path and failures.

verdicts.rationale: The decision journal (rankings and recruiter actions) is the automatically generated decision log. It is configured with retention_days: 400 and S3 Object Lock (E3), documented in ADR 0002 (E4), and stated in the privacy notice (E2, E11). Sample journal entries show the log exists (E5). 400 days is at least 180 days. The 14-day application logs in E4 are explicitly not the decision log. Retention is set by the bucket lifecycle rule at deploy time and the IaC for it isn't visible, but that is not a gap.
gaps: Bucket lifecycle/Object Lock IaC not visible in excerpts
instructions-for-use.md section 5 (Logs) is TBD
verdicts.remediation: Add the S3 bucket lifecycle and Object Lock definition (Terraform/CloudFormation) showing the 400-day retention. Complete the Logs section in docs/instructions-for-use.md.

verdicts.rationale: Recruiters (human users) can disregard or reverse the AI output through implemented mechanisms. The /override endpoint lets them move an application to another bucket, with a required justification. The /decision endpoint is the only way a candidate's status changes and needs a human recruiter [E1][E3]. The UI exposes Advance and Move actions and says the ranking is only a recommendation [E5]. Every override and decision is written to the append-only, object-locked DecisionJournal with actor, timestamp and result [E1][E2][E4]. A real log sample shows an override entry recorded [E8]. The instructions for use describe the same capability [E6].
verdicts.remediation: No action needed for this requirement. Optionally, complete the TBD sections in docs/instructions-for-use.md (performance/limitations, logs).

verdicts.rationale: An admin-only endpoint sets `automated_ranking_enabled = False` and journals a `suspended` event (E9). A matching resume endpoint exists (E9). When the flag is off, `/score` skips the model and marks the application unranked and "queued_for_manual_review" (E4). The instructions for use document this procedure: admins suspend ranking from the admin page and the queue falls back to chronological order (E8). The ADR lists the `suspended` and `resumed` events (E6). Together these show a kill switch that halts automated processing and routes cases to humans.
verdicts.remediation: No action is needed for this requirement. Optionally, persist the flag outside process memory so it applies to all pods and survives restarts.

verdicts.rationale: The decision flow shows the candidate status changes only through the /decision endpoint, which requires an authenticated recruiter and a written reason of at least 10 characters (E2, E3). The scoring endpoint only saves the ranking and never sets an adverse status. Parse failures and a suspended ranker produce an unranked, manual-review outcome and not a rejection (E2, E3, E7). The UI labels the ranking as an AI suggestion and says the recruiter makes the final decision. It also offers an override (E4). The risk register lists the automation-bias mitigation (E1), and the privacy notice states that no decision is made solely by automated means (E5). The deterministic pattern auto-reject is not evidenced in the excerpts.
verdicts.remediation: No action required. Optionally add a test that asserts no code path other than the /decision endpoint calls set_status.

verdicts.rationale: The model card (E2) declares accuracy levels with values for the hold-out set: NDCG@10 0.71, ROC-AUC 0.87, Precision@10 0.64 and Recall@50 0.82. It also gives a degraded-subgroup figure (AUC 0.79 for non-English CVs). The statement accepts a model card as the place for this declaration ('instructions for use and/or model card'). E1 and E3 support the figures with CI gate thresholds but are not the declaration themselves. The instructions for use (E7) still have 'Performance and limitations' as TBD. That does not defeat compliance, because the model card satisfies the statement.
gaps: Instructions for use (docs/instructions-for-use.md, section 4 'Performance and limitations') is still TBD and does not repeat the accuracy metrics that Art. 15(3) expects there.
verdicts.remediation: Complete section 4 of docs/instructions-for-use.md. Copy or reference the model card metrics (NDCG@10, ROC-AUC, Precision@10, Recall@50, and the lower non-English CV figure) so the deployer-facing instructions also declare them.

verdicts.rationale: The ranker wraps inference in a try block (E2) and the Ranking dataclass has a `needs_manual_review` flag and an optional score. That fits a fail-safe path to manual handling. The technical documentation says failures yield an unranked application rather than a low score (E9). The risk register says parse failures are routed unranked to the manual queue (E6). The API also has a kill switch that queues applications for manual review when automated ranking is suspended (E8). The model never accepts or rejects candidates, and status changes only through an explicit recruiter decision (E7, E4). So an error cannot produce an automatic adverse decision.
gaps: The except branch of Ranker.rank is cut off in the excerpt, so it is not visible that it returns score=None with needs_manual_review=True.
No visible timeout handling or test that covers model-unavailable or exception scenarios.
api.score does not visibly catch exceptions from ranker.rank.
verdicts.remediation: Add tests that simulate inference exceptions, timeouts and a missing model file, and assert that the result is an unranked application with needs_manual_review=True. Wrap the ranker.rank call in api.score with an explicit timeout and a fallback that queues the application for manual review. Document this fail-safe behaviour in docs/technical-documentation.md.

verdicts.rationale: The inference endpoint /applications/{id}/score takes a pydantic ScoreRequest, not a raw body (E7, E9). It has schema and type validation. Ranges are covered by experience_years ge=0, le=60. Size limits are covered by max_length on skills (200), languages (20) and summary (8000). The requisition_id regex and the Literal education_level enforce formats. Validation runs before ranker.rank(), and the endpoint is also authenticated (E1) and rate-limited (E7). Input is parsed CV text, so file-type checks are not relevant to the model input.
gaps: Individual skill/language string lengths are not bounded (list items unconstrained)
No visible overall request body size limit at the ingress
Upload file type/size validation for raw CV parsing is not shown
verdicts.remediation: Constrain list item lengths (e.g. list[constr(max_length=100)]). Add an ingress body-size limit (nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size). Validate file type and size in the CV parsing/upload path.

verdicts.rationale: E1 implements OIDC bearer-token authentication (JWT RS256 verified against a JWKS key, audience checked) with role-based authorisation (get_current_recruiter, require_role). E8 shows admin routes (/admin/ranking/resume) and the erasure route protected via require_role("screening-admin") and require_role("privacy-officer"). E5 shows TLS and an internal ingress, and E4 lists OIDC and RBAC as mitigations. The excerpts do not show the scoring/inference routes in api.py, so their protection is inferred rather than seen. Nothing in the excerpts shows an unauthenticated sensitive route.
gaps: Scoring/inference route decorators in api.py not visible, so their authentication is not directly confirmed
No evidence of rate limiting or adversarial-input protections (not required by the statement)
verdicts.remediation: Confirm that every route in api.py, including scoring and decision routes, depends on get_current_recruiter or require_role. Add a test that fails if any route lacks an auth dependency. Consider adding rate limiting at the ingress.

verdicts.rationale: E1 documents all four required procedures. It covers change management (PR with two approvals, governance sign-off, release notes). It covers pre-release validation (hold-out evaluation, a CI gate, shadow deployment, go/no-go). It covers post-market monitoring (weekly performance report, PSI drift alert at 0.2, quarterly override review). It covers incident reporting (triage, 24h escalation, Art. 73 notification to the authority by Legal). The procedures are backed by implementation: the CI gate in E8, the monitoring config in E4, and the drift risk R-02 in E5.
verdicts.remediation: No action needed for this requirement. Optionally, state review frequency for the procedures and link the group fairness evaluation (HR-412) into the pre-release validation gate.

verdicts.rationale: E1 is a CI quality gate with pytest assertions against predefined thresholds (ROC-AUC >= 0.85, NDCG@10 >= 0.68, unranked rate < 0.06) on a frozen hold-out report. E2 documents this gate as a mandatory pre-release validation step, alongside shadow deployment and go/no-go sign-off. E4 and E5 show the hold-out is a separate test split by requisition, and the model card reports results that meet the thresholds. The metrics fit the ranking purpose.
gaps: Instructions for use section 4 (performance) is TBD, but the statement does not require it
Fairness metrics are not part of the gate (fairness is out of scope for this requirement)
verdicts.remediation: Optionally add per-subgroup metric thresholds (for example non-English CVs, small requisitions) to the quality gate. Also have the pipeline generate holdout_report.json during CI so the gate always uses the release candidate.

verdicts.rationale: The privacy notice (E1) documents lawful bases for the candidate-assessment purpose: Art. 6(1)(b) pre-contractual steps and Art. 6(1)(f) legitimate interests. It names no lawful basis for the other purposes visible in the evidence. The datasheet (E2) says re-use of application data for model training was assessed in a LIA of 2025-11-03, but it doesn't name the basis, and the LIA itself isn't among the excerpts. The decision journal, which keeps rankings and decisions for 400 days (E7, E10), has no stated basis either. Consent isn't relied on, so recording it isn't needed. No record of processing or per-purpose mapping covers all purposes.
gaps: No documented lawful basis for model training and development on historical candidate data (only a reference to a LIA, not shown)
No documented lawful basis for the decision journal's 400-day retention of rankings and recruiter decisions
No record of processing activities or per-purpose lawful-basis mapping covering all purposes
The privacy notice lists a basis only for the application assessment purpose
verdicts.remediation: Add a record of processing (e.g. docs/ropa.md) that lists each purpose (application assessment, model training and evaluation, decision journal and audit retention, and any others) with its Art. 6(1) basis. Include the LIA of 2025-11-03 in the repository and reference it. Update docs/privacy-notice.md to state the purpose and basis for model training and for journal retention. If any purpose relies on consent, add a mechanism to collect and record it.

verdicts.rationale: E1 is a privacy notice that covers every element in the statement. It names the controller (ACME Corp, with address) and gives DPO contact details. It states the purposes and the lawful basis (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f)), the recipients, and the retention periods. It lists the rights to access, rectification, erasure, objection, and complaint to a supervisory authority. E1 is labelled as the excerpt shown on the careers portal, and E3 says candidates are informed through this notice. That supports the claim that it is shown or linked to data subjects at collection. The notice also discloses the AI ranking and says no decision is solely automated.
gaps: No code or UI evidence that the notice is actually displayed or linked at the point of application
Legitimate interests are only briefly stated
verdicts.remediation: Optionally add a link to docs/privacy-notice.md in the application form, with a test or config that shows it is displayed at collection. Also expand the legitimate-interest description.

verdicts.rationale: Retention periods are defined per data category in E1: raw CV 30 days, profile 180 days then anonymised, decision journal 400 days. They are enforced automatically by a nightly CronJob (E7, E8) running retention.py, which deletes raw CVs and anonymises profiles (E2). The journal is expired by a bucket lifecycle rule driven by the config value (E2, E4). The periods are proportionate to their purposes: short CV retention, a recruitment round plus challenge period for profiles, and the AI Act record-keeping period for the journal. The periods are also disclosed to candidates (E10).
gaps: The bucket lifecycle rule for the journal is not visible in the excerpts (IaC not shown)
No retention period is shown for the training dataset (DATASHEET.md), which is already stripped of direct identifiers
verdicts.remediation: Add the S3 lifecycle rule for the journal bucket to IaC, taking its value from decision_journal.retention_days. Add a retention statement for the training dataset in DATASHEET.md and config/retention.yaml.

verdicts.rationale: E1 shows an implemented on-request erasure endpoint (DELETE /candidates/{candidate_id}, restricted to the privacy-officer role). Its docstring says it deletes the CV, parsed profile and rankings via candidates.delete_everywhere, which covers the stores and derived data. The journal keeps only SHA-256 digests with no CV content (E1, E2), so it holds no directly identifying content. The nightly retention job (E3, E6, E8) is supplementary and not the erasure mechanism. The privacy notice (E5) lists the erasure right.
gaps: Implementation of delete_everywhere is not visible, so coverage of all stores and derived data is not verified
Object-locked journal entries keep a digest and actor/application id, and the excerpts do not show how these are handled on erasure
No documented time limit or SLA for handling erasure requests
verdicts.remediation: Document the erasure procedure and its SLA (for example one month). Add tests showing delete_everywhere removes the CV, profile, rankings, caches and backups. Confirm that journal entries tied to the application id cannot identify the candidate after erasure.

verdicts.rationale: No significant decision is solely automated. The only way a candidate's status changes is the /decision endpoint, which requires an authenticated human recruiter (E1). The ranking is advisory: recruiters can override it (E1, E3), and the UI states that the recruiter makes the final decision (E5). Instructions require every candidate to be opened and rejections to carry a written reason (E6). The privacy notice states that no decision is made solely by automated means (E2). The journal shows human actors on all decisions (E4, E8). Because the decision is not solely automated, an Art. 22(3) contest path is not required.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: add a candidate-facing channel to request review of a decision, and complete the TBD sections of docs/instructions-for-use.md.

verdicts.rationale: The candidate-facing privacy notice [E1] says an AI system ranks applications. It gives the main factors: skills, experience and education matched to the role. It says which attributes are not used. It states the consequence: a recruiter reviews every application and takes all decisions, and no decision is solely automated. That covers the existence of the AI ranking, meaningful information about the logic, and its envisaged consequences. It is aimed at data subjects rather than being internal documentation. The recruiter UI [E3] and the instructions [E5] are internal and add nothing to this finding.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: add to docs/privacy-notice.md that the ranking only affects the order of review, and add a sentence on how candidates can ask for human review of, or contest, their outcome.

verdicts.rationale: The ranker code defines REDACTED_FIELDS (name, email, phone, photo, date of birth, gender, nationality, address) and a redact() method that is applied before build_features, so protected attributes are never model features [E4]. The datasheet shows these fields were removed before storage in the training bucket and candidate ids were replaced by salted hashes, which is pseudonymisation [E1]. The technical documentation and privacy notice are consistent with this [E2][E6]. No third-party LLM or raw-data sharing is evidenced; recipients are only recruiters and the EU AWS host [E6]. The missing bias evaluation is a fairness issue, not a minimisation one, so it doesn't change this assessment.
verdicts.remediation: No action needed for this requirement. Optionally, add a test that asserts redact() removes all REDACTED_FIELDS, and document how proxy features are reviewed.

verdicts.rationale: In transit: the Ingress terminates TLS with a cert-manager certificate from an internal CA, and re-encrypts to the backend over HTTPS on port 8443 with a mounted TLS secret (E2, E3). At rest: the EBS StorageClass has encrypted=true with a KMS key (E3), and the S3 decision journal is written with SSE-KMS (E1). Some stores that hold personal data show no encryption evidence. These are the raw CV and candidate profile stores (E9), the training bucket (E7), and any database or backup. The journal bucket's default encryption and the S3 TLS enforcement are not evidenced in IaC either. So the evidence is only partial for all stores.
gaps: No encryption-at-rest evidence for the raw CV / candidate profile storage (E9) or any database
No encryption evidence for the training dataset bucket s3://acme-hireright-datasets (E7)
No evidence of backup encryption
No bucket-level default encryption or TLS-only bucket policy (aws:SecureTransport) in IaC
No evidence of TLS for connections to the database, Workday/ATS bridge, or other internal services
verdicts.remediation: Add IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation) that shows SSE-KMS default encryption on all S3 buckets holding personal data (CV, profile, journal, datasets), with a bucket policy that denies non-TLS requests. Show encrypted databases and backups (for example RDS with storage_encrypted and a KMS key, and encrypted snapshots). Ensure PVCs use the gp3-encrypted StorageClass. Document TLS settings for the ATS bridge and DB connections, and add a short encryption inventory to the technical documentation that lists each store and its protection.

verdicts.rationale: E1 implements OIDC bearer-token authentication with RS256 JWT validation, audience check and role checks (recruiter or screening-admin), plus a require_role helper for least privilege. E6 shows admin routes (suspend/resume ranking) restricted to screening-admin and the erasure endpoint restricted to privacy-officer. E10 shows decision and override endpoints require an authenticated recruiter. E3 and E7 show TLS on the ingress. The visible endpoints all enforce authentication and role-based authorisation. Excerpts are partial, so any other routes are not visible, but nothing shows an unauthenticated endpoint.
verdicts.remediation: No change required. Optionally add a test that every route in api.py declares an auth dependency, and verify the remaining routes not shown (e.g. candidate read/list) use get_current_recruiter or require_role.

verdicts.rationale: No ROPA artefact appears in the excerpts. The README documentation list (E2) names no ROPA or processing-record file. The privacy notice (E7) has the controller, DPO, purposes, recipients and retention periods. It is a candidate-facing notice, not a maintained record. It also lacks data subject and data category descriptions, transfer information and security measures. The risk assessment (E5) mentions security controls such as KMS, RBAC and OIDC only as risk mitigations. Related fragments in other documents do not amount to a record of processing activities.
gaps: No ROPA document (markdown/yaml) in the repository
No consolidated list of categories of data subjects and personal data
No statement on third-country transfers (AWS EU region is only mentioned in passing)
No consolidated description of technical and organisational security measures
No controller/DPO contact details in a record, joint controller or representative not addressed
verdicts.remediation: Add docs/ropa.md (or ropa.yaml) with an Art. 30(1) entry for HireRight Screening. It should cover: controller and DPO contacts; purposes (recruitment screening and ranking, model training under the LIA); data subjects (job candidates); personal data categories (parsed CV, structured profile, scores, journal entries); recipients (recruiters, hiring managers, AWS as processor); third-country transfers, or an explicit statement that there are none; retention periods (CV 30 days, profile 180 days, journal 400 days); and security measures (OIDC, RBAC, KMS encryption, S3 Object Lock, network policies). Link it from the README and review it on a schedule.

verdicts.rationale: No DPIA document appears in the excerpts. The README lists the documentation set (model card, datasheet, technical documentation, instructions, release process) and none is a DPIA (E2). The risk register in docs/risk-assessment.md is an AI Act classification and risk document (E3). It does not cover the Art. 35(7) elements: a systematic description of the processing, a necessity and proportionality assessment, and an assessment of risks to data subjects' rights. The privacy notice mentions a LIA for training-data re-use (E5) and a legal basis (E7), but these are fragments and not a DPIA. The system profiles candidates, so a DPIA would be expected.
gaps: No DPIA document exists
No necessity and proportionality assessment
No assessment of risks to data subjects' rights and freedoms under GDPR
No documented consultation with the DPO or data subjects
Processing description and mitigations are not consolidated in an Art. 35(7) structure
verdicts.remediation: Add docs/dpia.md, completed before further processing and approved by the DPO. It should cover: (a) a systematic description of the processing (data categories, flows ATS to ranker to journal, retention, recipients, purposes, and the legitimate interest); (b) a necessity and proportionality assessment, including alternatives and data minimisation; (c) a risk assessment for data subjects (profiling, bias, automation bias, access); (d) mitigations and safeguards (human review, removal of protected fields, encryption, retention, rights handling). Link it from the README and reference the LIA of 2025-11-03 and the risk register. Complete the pending fairness evaluation HR-412 and feed it into the DPIA. Schedule periodic review.

verdicts.rationale: The only AI-facing interface in the evidence is the recruiter dashboard. In E1, CandidateRanking.tsx shows a visible, non-tooltip notice above the table. It reads "AI-suggested ranking... a recommendation produced by an AI model" and says "You, the recruiter, make the final decision for every candidate." That meets both the AI-disclosure element and the decision-support element (AI recommendation plus who decides). E2 and E6 confirm the dashboard is the only UI and that the ranking is a recommendation. E4 discloses AI use to candidates on the careers portal.
verdicts.remediation: No action required. Optionally, check that any e-mail or notification templates also disclose AI involvement.

verdicts.rationale: Applies to limited risk systems; this system is classified as high.

The API writes a "ranked" DecisionJournal entry for each production scoring call (E5). Each entry carries a UTC timestamp (`at`), a unique entry_id, model_version, an input_digest (SHA-256 reference, not raw CV), the result (score and reasons) and the actor (E7). Entries are appended to an S3 bucket with Object Lock in compliance mode (WORM), which is tamper-resistant (E2, E6, E7). Retention is set to 400 days, above the 180-day minimum (E2, E4), and the bucket lifecycle takes its value from that setting (E3).
gaps: The correlation id is the per-entry entry_id and application_id. No request-level correlation id propagated from the incoming request is visible.
The bucket lifecycle and Object Lock retention are not shown in IaC. They are only described as being applied at deploy time.
verdicts.remediation: Optionally add a request correlation id (e.g. an X-Request-ID header) to JournalEntry. Add the S3 bucket's Object Lock and lifecycle configuration to IaC, with retention of at least 180 days, so the 400-day setting is verifiable.

verdicts.rationale: Raw CVs (uploaded files and parsed text) have retention_days: 30 in the retention schedule [E1]. A nightly Kubernetes CronJob runs the retention job [E9][E10], and that job deletes raw documents older than the configured cutoff [E2]. This meets the 30-day limit and the automation requirement. The structured profile is kept 180 days but is anonymised afterwards [E1][E2]. It is a processed profile, not a raw input. The decision journal keeps 400 days but holds only SHA-256 digests and no CV content [E4][E7], so it is not a raw personal-data store. The privacy notice matches these periods [E8].
verdicts.remediation: No change is required. Optionally, document explicitly that the 180-day candidate profile contains no raw inputs. Also confirm that other raw stores, such as ATS bridge payloads, are covered by the purge.

verdicts.rationale: Transit encryption is evidenced: the ingress uses TLS with cert-manager, backend-protocol HTTPS, and the pod serves on 8443 with mounted TLS certs (E1, E2). At rest, the EBS StorageClass is encrypted with a KMS key (E1), and the decision journal is written to S3 with aws:kms server-side encryption (E7). The training dataset bucket (personal-data derived, E3) and model artefacts have no visible encryption config. The excerpts also don't show a minimum TLS version of 1.2 or higher, or that the internal service-to-service traffic is covered. Coverage is therefore incomplete on both elements.
gaps: No evidence of encryption at rest for the S3 training/dataset bucket (acme-hireright-datasets)
No evidence of encryption at rest for model artefact storage
No explicit TLS minimum version (1.2+) configured
No evidence that service-to-service traffic (e.g. ats-bridge) uses TLS
Only the journal and the EBS StorageClass are shown as encrypted; coverage of the other stores is not shown
verdicts.remediation: Add IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation) showing SSE-KMS with default bucket encryption for the dataset, model-artefact and journal buckets. Make sure PVCs use the gp3-encrypted StorageClass. Set ssl-protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 (or ssl-min-version) on the ingress and in the app's TLS settings. Enforce mTLS or TLS for internal calls, for example to ats-bridge, and document this in the technical documentation.

verdicts.rationale: E2 implements OIDC bearer-token authentication with `get_current_recruiter`, which returns 401 on an invalid token and 403 without the right role. It also defines a `require_role(role)` dependency for role-based authorisation. In E6, the visible routes (`/decision`, `/override`, and the ranking route that records `actor=user.id`) all depend on `get_current_recruiter`, so none is unauthenticated. E10 configures a rate limit of 120/minute and the roles recruiter, screening-admin and privacy-officer. E3 lists OIDC auth and RBAC as mitigations. The README (E7) says `api.py` contains admin controls and erasure. The excerpts don't show those admin routes, so I can't confirm they call `require_role`. Since the excerpts are truncated, I'm not treating that as a gap. No unauthenticated route and no admin route without a role check appears in the evidence.
gaps: The admin routes (model reload, threshold change, data export, erasure) are not shown, so `require_role('screening-admin')` on them is unconfirmed.
The excerpts don't show where the rate limit is enforced or whether any public routes are declared.
verdicts.remediation: Make sure every admin route in `src/hireright/api.py` (model reload, threshold changes, data export, transcript access, erasure) uses `Depends(require_role('screening-admin'))` or the privacy-officer role as appropriate. Add tests that check a recruiter-only token gets 403 on these routes. Confirm that the `rate_limit` setting in `config/app.yaml` is enforced in middleware, and declare any intentionally public route explicitly in the config.

verdicts.rationale: Candidate status changes only through the /decision endpoint, which requires an authenticated recruiter (E2). The decision requires an outcome (advance/reject/hold) and a written reason of at least 10 characters (E3). The journal records a `reviewer_decision` event with the actor (E2, E6). The UI shows the AI score and main reasons, labels the ranking as a suggestion, and lets the recruiter decide or override (E4). The score endpoint only ranks and saves the result. Parse failures go unranked to a manual queue, not to rejection (E1, E3). The README states that the system never rejects on its own (E7), and no auto-reject pattern appears in the excerpts.
gaps: No check visible that the reviewer actually viewed the AI output before approving (the journal logs the decision but not the displayed output)
Reviewer training is only mentioned as a mitigation in the risk register, with no evidence it is enforced
verdicts.remediation: Include the model version and score or reasons shown to the reviewer in the reviewer_decision journal entry, so the log ties the approval to the AI output. Add a test that proves no code path other than /decision can set a reject status.

verdicts.rationale: MODEL_CARD.md [E3] covers every field the statement lists. It gives intended use and out-of-scope uses, the model version (`ranker-2.4.1`), a training data summary (512k triples, 2021-2025, linked to DATASHEET.md [E5]), evaluation metrics (NDCG@10, AUC, P@10, R@50), limitations, and the owner (Talent Data Science). The deployed model in config [E7] and code [E9] is `ranker-2.4.1`, which matches the card. No third-party models appear in the excerpts. The pending fairness evaluation is noted in the card, but the statement does not require it.
verdicts.remediation: No action needed for this requirement. Optionally, add a third-party model card (provider, version, product-specific evaluation) if any external model is introduced. Keep MODEL_CARD.md in sync with each release.

verdicts.rationale: The API configures a slowapi `Limiter` keyed per client by remote address, with `default_limits` read from settings (E6). The limit is defined in configuration as `rate_limit: "120/minute"` (E1). The service is deployed as an internal REST API behind an internal-host ingress (E3, E8), so it may not be reachable from untrusted networks. The rate limiting is in place either way. The excerpt does not show the `SlowAPIMiddleware` or the exception handler, but it is cut off at 40 lines, so I do not count that as a gap.
gaps: SlowAPIMiddleware or per-route decorators are not visible in the excerpts, so enforcement is not directly confirmed
The key function uses the remote IP, which may resolve to the ingress address behind a proxy unless forwarded headers are handled
verdicts.remediation: Confirm that `SlowAPIMiddleware` is added (`app.add_middleware(SlowAPIMiddleware)`) and that a `RateLimitExceeded` handler is registered. Make sure the client IP comes from trusted forwarded headers, or key on the authenticated principal id. Optionally add an nginx ingress annotation such as `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps` as a second layer.

verdicts.rationale: E1 has an "Incident reporting" section in docs/release-process.md. It covers AI incidents (discriminatory behaviour, data leak, severe degradation). They are raised in #hireright-incidents, triaged by the on-call ML engineer and reported to the AI Governance Board (ai-incidents@acme.example) within 24 hours. This covers the 24h reporting and escalation to the board, and it mentions Art. 73 notification by Legal. However, it is a short paragraph inside a release document, not a dedicated incident response procedure. Detection is only implied by the drift alerts in E1 and E4. The excerpts do not define "serious" incidents or the safety-event category. They also give no steps, roles or severity criteria.
gaps: No dedicated AI incident response procedure document
Detection steps not described as part of an incident procedure
No definition or criteria for 'serious' incidents versus other incidents
Safety events not listed among incident types
No defined roles, severity levels or escalation steps beyond triage

# HireRight Screening

HireRight Screening ranks incoming job applications for ACME Talent Acquisition so recruiters can
prioritise their review queue. The model reads the parsed CV and the job requisition and produces a
relevance score (0-1) plus the main reasons behind it. **Recruiters take every decision**; the
system never rejects or advances a candidate on its own.

## Regulatory position

* EU AI Act: **high-risk AI system** under Annex III, point 4(a) (AI systems intended to be used to
  analyse and filter job applications and to evaluate candidates). ACME acts as provider and deployer.
  See `docs/risk-assessment.md` for the classification rationale and the risk register.
* GDPR: ACME is controller; candidates are informed through `docs/privacy-notice.md`.

## Components

|---|---|
| `src/hireright/api.py` | FastAPI service: scoring, reviewer decisions, admin controls, erasure |
| `src/hireright/model.py` | Gradient-boosted ranker + per-candidate explanations |
| `src/hireright/journal.py` | `DecisionJournal`, append-only record of every score and human action |
| `src/hireright/retention.py` | Nightly purge of raw CVs and expired journal segments |
| `web/` | Recruiter dashboard (React) |
| `infra/k8s/` | Deployment manifests (EKS) |

## Documentation

* `MODEL_CARD.md`, `DATASHEET.md`
* `docs/technical-documentation.md` (Annex IV structure)
* `docs/instructions-for-use.md` (for recruiting teams)
* `docs/release-process.md` (change management, monitoring, incidents)

# Datasheet: HireRight ranking dataset v5

## 1. Motivation
Built to train and evaluate the candidate ranker (`MODEL_CARD.md`).

## 2. Composition
* 512,340 (application, requisition, label) triples; 38,912 requisitions; 14 EU countries.
* Label: 1 if a recruiter shortlisted the application, else 0.
* Splits: train 2021-01..2024-12 (80%), validation 2025-H1 (10%), test 2025-H2 (10%), split by
  requisition to avoid leakage.

## 3. Collection and personal data
* Source: ACME ATS (Workday) exports; original purpose of collection: recruitment for the
  advertised role. Re-use for model development assessed in the LIA of 2025-11-03.
* Removed before storage in the training bucket: name, e-mail, phone, photo, date of birth, gender,
  nationality, address. Candidate ids are replaced by salted hashes.

## 4. Preparation
* CV parsing with `cvparse 3.2`; documents failing parsing (4.1%) were dropped.
* Deduplication of re-applications within 30 days; skill normalisation against ESCO v1.2.
* Label noise review on a 2,000-sample audit (agreement 0.91).

## 5. Assumptions and known gaps
* Assumes recruiter shortlisting is a reasonable proxy for relevance.
* Under-representation of applications for engineering roles in DE/AT before 2023.
* Bias examination: not yet performed on this version (ticket HR-412, planned for Q4 2026).

## 6. Maintenance
Refreshed yearly by Talent Data Science; versions stored in `s3://acme-hireright-datasets/`.

# Risk assessment and AI Act classification

## Classification
HireRight Screening is intended to "analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate
candidates" and therefore falls under **Annex III, point 4(a)** of the AI Act. The Art. 6(3)
derogation does not apply: the ranking materially influences which candidates are reviewed first,
and the system profiles natural persons. **Result: high-risk.**

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| R-05 | Unauthorised access to candidate data | low | high | OIDC auth, RBAC, KMS encryption, network policies | low |

Every change to the model, features, thresholds or UI text goes through a pull request with two
approvals (one from Talent Data Science, one from Talent Technology). Model releases additionally
require sign-off by the AI Governance Board representative. Release notes record the model version

# HireRight Screening: technical documentation (AI Act Art. 11, Annex IV)

## 1. General description
* **Intended purpose:** ranking job applications per requisition to support recruiters at ACME.
  Provider and deployer: ACME Corp, Talent Technology. System version 2.4.1 (model `ranker-2.4.1`),
  previous version 2.3.0 used a logistic-regression scorer.
* **Interaction with other systems:** consumes parsed CVs from the ATS (Workday) through the
  `ats-bridge` service; returns rankings to the recruiter dashboard. No other AI systems are called.
* **Software versions:** Python 3.12, LightGBM 4.3, SHAP 0.45, FastAPI 0.111.
* **Forms of deployment:** internal REST API on EKS (eu-central-1); not sold externally.
* **Hardware:** 2x c7g.xlarge pods; no GPU required.
* **User interface:** recruiter dashboard (`web/`) showing ranking, main reasons and actions.

## 2. Development process and design
* **Methods:** supervised learning-to-rank (LambdaRank) on historical shortlisting decisions;
  hyper-parameters tuned with 5-fold group CV by requisition.
* **Design choices:** decision support only; protected attributes and identity fields removed
  before feature extraction; per-candidate SHAP explanations exposed to recruiters; failures yield

* **Validation and testing:** offline evaluation on hold-out (see `MODEL_CARD.md`), CI quality gate

## 3. Monitoring and control
Weekly performance report and PSI-based drift alerts (`config/app.yaml: monitoring`).

## 4. Risk management
See `docs/risk-assessment.md`.

"""Candidate ranker: LightGBM LambdaRank model over CV/requisition features, with explanations."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass

import lightgbm as lgb
import numpy as np
import shap

from .features import build_features

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MODEL_VERSION = "ranker-2.4.1"
# Fields removed before feature extraction: identity and protected characteristics are never
# visible to the model (data minimisation, see DATASHEET.md section 3).
REDACTED_FIELDS = ("name", "email", "phone", "photo", "date_of_birth", "gender", "nationality", "address")


@dataclass
class Ranking:
    score: float | None
    reasons: list[tuple[str, float]]
    model_version: str
    needs_manual_review: bool = False


class Ranker:
    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self.booster = lgb.Booster(model_file=path)
        self.explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(self.booster)

    @staticmethod
    def redact(cv: dict) -> dict:
        return {k: v for k, v in cv.items() if k not in REDACTED_FIELDS}

    def rank(self, cv: dict, requisition: dict) -> Ranking:
        try:
            x = build_features(self.redact(cv), requisition)
            score = float(self.booster.predict(np.array([x]))[0])
            contrib = self.explainer.shap_values(np.array([x]))[0]
            names = self.booster.feature_name()
            top = sorted(zip(names, contrib), key=lambda t: abs(t[1]), reverse=True)[:5]
            return Ranking(score=score, reasons=[(n, float(c)) for n, c in top], model_version=MODEL_VERSION)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            # Fallback: never guess. The application goes to the recruiter queue unranked.
            log.exception("ranker failed; application queued unranked")
            return Ranking(score=None, reasons=[], model_version=MODEL_VERSION, needs_manual_review=True)

# ADR 0002: DecisionJournal instead of application logs for traceability

* Status: accepted (2025-09-18)

## Context
We need a reliable trace of every ranking and every human action (AI Act Art. 12, 19 and 26(6)).
Application logs are sampled, mutable and expire after 14 days in our logging platform.

## Decision
Introduce `DecisionJournal` (`src/hireright/journal.py`): one JSON entry per event (`ranked`,
`reviewer_decision`, `override`, `suspended`, `resumed`) with model version, input digest, result and
actor, written to an S3 bucket with Object Lock in compliance mode. Retention: 400 days
(`config/retention.yaml`). CV content is never written to the journal; only a SHA-256 digest.

## Consequences
* Auditors can reconstruct who saw which ranking and what was decided.
* Journal lines are not visible in Kibana; a small Athena view is provided for investigations.

"""Nightly retention job (CronJob `hireright-retention`, see infra/k8s/deployment.yaml)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import yaml

from .store import candidates, s3


def run(config_path: str = "config/retention.yaml") -> dict[str, int]:
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(config_path))
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    removed = {}
    raw_cutoff = now - timedelta(days=cfg["raw_cv"]["retention_days"])
    removed["raw_cv"] = candidates.delete_raw_documents(older_than=raw_cutoff)
    profile_cutoff = now - timedelta(days=cfg["candidate_profile"]["retention_days"])
    removed["profiles"] = candidates.anonymise_profiles(older_than=profile_cutoff)
    # Journal segments are object-locked; expiry is handled by the bucket lifecycle rule whose
    # value is taken from decision_journal.retention_days at deploy time.
    return removed
